t: 3500. Minimum Cost to Divide Array Into Subarrays
o: Split nums into ordered contiguous subarrays; the i-th subarray nums[l..r] costs (prefixNums[r] + k·i) × (sum of cost[l..r]). Both examples confirm the formula. With n up to 1000 and k up to 1000, an O(n²k) DP is too slow, but the transition is linear in the split point's cost-prefix, so convex-hull optimization reduces it to O(n²) overall (k layers, each with an amortized-linear hull).
k: dp[j][i] = min cost splitting the first i elements into j parts; the last part starts at l+1.
Cost = dp[j-1][l] + (pre[i] + k·j)·(cs[i] − cs[l]), linear in cs[l] → treat each candidate as a line and query at x = pre[i] + k·j.
Within a layer, slopes −cs[l] decrease and queries x increase, so a monotone CHT with a forward-moving pointer works in amortized O(1) per step.

a.i: Define dp[j][i] and try every last-split point l. This directly mirrors the cost definition and is easy to verify against the examples, but at O(n²·k) ≈ 10⁹ it exceeds limits for the largest inputs — still worth presenting first.
s: Compute prefix sums pre of nums and cs of cost.
dp[0][0] = 0; for j = 1..n, i = j..n, minimize over l of dp[j-1][l] + (pre[i]+k·j)·(cs[i]-cs[l]).
a.t: O(n³) worst case (n² splits × n candidates) — TLE for large n

a.n: Approach 2: Layered DP with monotone Convex Hull Trick
a.i: Rewrite the transition as dp[j-1][l] − (pre[i]+k·j)·cs[l] + (pre[i]+k·j)·cs[i]. Each l defines a line y = (−cs[l])·x + dp[j-1][l]; querying at x = pre[i]+k·j gives the best split. Since cs is increasing (slopes added in decreasing order) and x increases within each layer, the classic monotone hull with a head pointer answers each query amortized in O(1).
s: Precompute prefix sums pre and cs; roll dp over layers j = 1..n.
Per layer, sweep i upward: insert line (m = −cs[i-1], b = dp_prev[i-1]) maintaining hull convexity via the cross-product bad test, then query at x = pre[i] + k·j advancing the pointer.
Add (pre[i]+k·j)·cs[i] to the query result; answer is dp after layer n at index n.
a.t: O(n²) total — n layers, each with amortized O(1) hull insert/query per index
a.sp: O(n) rolling DP plus hull storage

w: Present the plain DP first (it validates understanding against the samples), then optimize with CHT — the tag list literally hints 'Li Chao Tree', and the monotone hull is a lighter equivalent here because both slopes and queries are monotone per layer. Critical detail: the k·j term belongs inside the multiplier, so the query point changes per layer — reset the hull and pointer each layer. Overflow: values reach ~(2·10⁶)·(10⁶) ≈ 2·10¹², so use 64-bit integers everywhere. Follow-up: what if cost could be negative? Then the monotonicity argument breaks and you'd need a full Li Chao tree or divide-and-conquer optimization.
